title: A Lidar Scan to Points: Ranges Become Points in the Sensor's Frame and Then in the Vehicle's, and What the Gaps Between Them Hide

questions.question: What should a beam that saw nothing give?
options: A point at the sensor's maximum range
The same point as the beam before it
questions.explanation: Any point is a claim that something is there. A beam with no return, or one outside the sensor's limits, has to give nothing, or the next stage sees a wall.

questions.question: A scan of 360 beams of a room gave how many points?
questions.explanation: Every beam had a range inside the limits, so each gave a point. With a tenth of the beams lost the same scan gave 325.

questions.question: With one degree between beams, at 10 m the points were:
questions.explanation: One degree is 0.01745 rad, and neighbouring points are the range times that apart: 0.175 m at 10 m.

questions.question: A post 0.3 m wide is hit by two beams at most how far away?
questions.explanation: Two beams hit it while the points are no further apart than its width. 0.3 m over 0.01745 rad is 17.2 m.

questions.question: Why are the points of a flat wall at different heights when the sensor is tipped?
options: The wall is not flat at that scale
The beams are refracted near the floor
The ranges are noisier for a tipped sensor
questions.explanation: Beams to the front are lowered and beams behind raised. Tipped down 5 degrees, the scan plane cuts the wall ahead lower and the wall behind higher. Taken through the mount's transform the heights ran from -0.19 to 0.69 m.

questions.question: Why is a sensor's range on its data sheet not the range at which a post is seen?
options: It is for a large flat target; a narrow thing needs two beams, and they spread with range
The data sheet is for indoor use
A post reflects less light than a wall
The range depends on the beam's power, not the target
questions.explanation: The quoted range is for something large. A post has to be hit by two beams to be seen, and beyond 17.2 m a one degree lidar hits it with one or none.
